note: Written before the run. Shape follows check_predictions.displacement_checks: each entry becomes one add(name, verdict, observed, threshold, note) row. The dispatch entry in CHECKS is deliberately NOT added here -- the coordinator wires `episodic_reset` -> episodic_reset_checks after all three iteration-2 candidates land, to avoid a collision with proposers 2a and 2b.
brief_corrections: The brief's claim that A4 has never fired is false: displacement (iter1) produced n_errors=35, trustworthy=true, rc_ratio=1.2575. The A4 bar is therefore raised from n_errors>=30 to n_errors>=150.

rc_ratio is bounded by the model's relation_count distribution at a given error count (max 1.2525 at 12 errors, 1.2575 at 35, 1.2879 at 150, 1.3750 at 400). displacement's 1.2575 was exactly its ceiling (rc_mean_error = 10.000), so it carries no information beyond 'all errors were late'. 1.386 needs several hundred errors.

variable_mapping is scored by DIFFERENT FORMULAS on the two sides: human = correct-count/10, model = relation_count of the last correct question before the first error, /10. relation_count = min(2q,10) saturates at q5, so errors at q6-q10 are invisible to the model's score. This is a fifth comparability defect and is not in the audit table.

interference.py:model_trials under-counts assigned_before by ~2x (assignment turns run 1..20 against question_index 1..10, two assignments per question, but the filter keeps only k-1), biasing intrusion_share downward. No threshold is registered on intrusion_share for that reason.

predictions.name: variable_mapping A4 n_errors >= 150
predictions.note: 674/1500 questions (45%) ask about a name the store has evicted and are answered at 0.985 from history. With the store as the only route those must fall toward the 4-option chance rate of 0.25, giving an expected error rate near 0.34; threshold set well below at 0.10. Below 75 errors the store was never needed and the leak reading is wrong.

predictions.name: variable_mapping A4 rc_ratio > 1.15 (interference-structured, not noise)
predictions.note: ACCEPTED AS DISCONFIRMING: 150+ errors with rc_ratio <= 1.15 means errors are uniform over question index -- the model was made noisy, not memory-limited. Honest reading of a pass: for the model, relation_count is collinear with question index, so this says errors are concentrated late, which is necessary but not sufficient for an interference account. Attainable ceiling at 150 errors is 1.2879.

predictions.name: share of variable_mapping runs with first_error_at <= 5 rises above 0.25
predictions.quantity: fraction of rows with metrics.first_error_at is not None and <= 5
predictions.point_estimate_basis: 1 - 0.66^5 at a per-question error rate of 0.34; the 0.25 threshold is a deliberate lower bound and will not discriminate a strong result from a marginal one -- read the observed value against the point estimate
predictions.note: This is the quantity the model's variable_mapping score actually depends on, because score = relation_count of the last correct question and relation_count = min(2q,10) saturates at q5. It cannot be bought by late errors, which is what distinguishes this candidate from displacement.

predictions.name: variable_mapping ceiling point mass breaks up
predictions.disconfirm_if: point mass intact (fraction at 1.0 >= 0.95), which would contradict P1 and P3
predictions.note: Weaker proxy for P3; retained because the brief asked for a point-mass prediction explicitly. Direction: downward in the share at ceiling, upward in distinct values.

predictions.name: variable_mapping humanlikeness rises by at least 0.05

either.reads_as: with P1 passing, the score formula is absorbing the errors -- apply protocol_match_rule before interpreting
overshot the human mean of 0.394; the model is now WORSE than humans on this task, which is overshoot, not calibration

predictions.note: Triggers the A4 conditional guard in score_candidate.py; P1 and P2 are the pre-commitment to pass it. The 0.05 threshold is nine times below the point estimate and is a floor, not a forecast.

predictions.name: n=3 store starts carrying letter identity
predictions.quantity: share of n=3 final_kv values containing a bare capital letter, regex (?<![A-Za-z])[A-Z](?![A-Za-z])
predictions.note: The decisive mechanism test on nback and the strongest single number in the diagnosis: at baseline the n=3 store holds NO letters (0.020) while acc_over_answered is 0.7372, which a 4-slot store cannot support -- so those answers came from history. Cannot be bought by guessing or by breaking output parsing. Same 0.020 under displacement, so displacement's n=3 HL of 0.9387 is leak-derived and is about response production, not a load-bearing store.

predictions.name: n=3 keys_held direction (branch discriminator, reported not thresholded)
predictions.quantity: keys_held at n=3, read jointly with P6 and with answered
predictions.note: Branches stated in advance. (a) P6 passes and keys_held falls toward 1 => the agent adopted full_context's rolling single-key strategy, which never overflows and so never meets the refusal; nback may improve, for the right reason. Considered most likely. (b) P6 passes but keys_held stays ~4 and answered falls => the refuse-on-full jam dominates; nback regresses and closing the leak needs proposer 2a's overflow fix to be viable. Informative either way, not a refutation.

predictions.name: variable_mapping output format intact (parse-integrity guard)
predictions.quantity: count of questions whose parsed answer is missing or not a valid option letter
predictions.source: tasks/wm_variable_mapping.jsonl -> parsed_answers vs questions[].options; equals interference.py's selected is None case
predictions.note: interference.py counts an unparsed answer as a novel_guess ERROR, so a candidate that reached P1 by emitting garbage would inflate n_errors while failing here. Replaces an intrusion_share threshold, which is unsafe given the assigned_before bug reported in brief_corrections.

predictions.name: n=1 nback unaffected (the confusion / parsing test)
predictions.note: THE KEY TEST. At n=1 a single overwritten key suffices and the baseline already uses exactly that (previous_letter in 50/50 blocks, keys_held 1.00). One item in four slots cannot be a capacity failure, so a drop here can only mean the reset broke instruction-following, phase tracking or output parsing. A P9 FAILURE INVALIDATES P1-P7 REGARDLESS OF THEIR VALUES.

predictions.name: six tasks byte-identical (no-change control)
predictions.quantity: per-task humanlikeness delta, and the A1/A2/A3 axis values
predictions.note: Structural, not statistical, and VERIFIED OFFLINE: encode() calls step() exactly once and all six tasks build a fresh agent per trial (wm_digit_span_forward.py:209, wm_digit_span_reverse.py:110, wm_semantic_story_recall.py:165, wm_mcq_common.py:52, wm_word_recognition.py:94), so on that single step there is no history to drop and the store is empty, so no state block is prepended. A stub-LLM test confirms the encode()->recall() request stream is byte-for-byte equal to baseline's. Expected delta is EXACTLY 0; any nonzero movement is serving nondeterminism and must not be narrated as a mechanism effect. Corollary: the mean can only move via nback and variable_mapping.

predictions.name: mean humanlikeness (not the primary claim)
predictions.derivation: Conditioned rather than guessed, because P5's point estimate of +0.45 to +0.55 on variable_mapping is worth +0.056 to +0.069 on the 8-task mean by itself (divide by 8). Branch (a) of P7 adds roughly a further +0.019 from nback. An unconditional range would have been miscalibrated the way iteration 1's word_recognition threshold was.
predictions.note: This candidate is not proposed as a score improvement. It is proposed as the run that makes nback and variable_mapping measure the memory module. A branch-(a) mean gain would be the largest in the search so far and must NOT be read as a capability result -- it is what happens when two tasks stop being scored on a leak, and its variable_mapping component is not interpretable until protocol_match_rule is applied.

accepted_costs.statement: No improvement is predicted and a floor violation is a live possibility. Refuse-on-full is still in place and proposer 2a owns that surface. The baseline's n=3 acc_over_answered of 0.7372 is leak-derived (see P6), so a fall there is the leak closing, not the model breaking; P9 is the test that distinguishes the two.

protocol_match_rule.where: analysis side only -- protocol_match.py, NOT the harness; a harness must not know the scoring protocol
protocol_match_rule.rule: Recompute each model run's variable_mapping score as (number of questions answered correctly) / 10, i.e. the same formula src/score.py:_score_human_record applies to humans, replacing metrics['score'] = relation_count of the last question answered correctly before the first error. Score both sides that way and recompute humanlikeness.
protocol_match_rule.why: The two sides currently use different formulas that share a denominator. relation_count = min(2q,10) saturates at q5, so an error at q6-q10 is invisible to the model's score: the baseline's first_error_at histogram is {3:2, 8:4, 9:2, 10:4} and 10 of the 12 runs with an error still score 1.0.
protocol_match_rule.three_strike_rule: INERT, do not apply. Truncating model runs at the third strike leaves 1495 of 1500 trials (mean 9.97 of 10 questions answered) and moves rc_ratio only from 1.2575 to 1.2586. Worth reporting the truncated question count as a covariate under this candidate, since error rates should rise enough for the rule to start biting.

interactions.2b_word_recognition: RESOLVED BY INSPECTION, not guessed: candidates/serial_recognition/harness.py overrides recall() only and keeps word_recognition on the encode()->recall() route. So the two mechanisms are ORTHOGONAL -- under this candidate alone word_recognition does not move (P10, verified byte-identical), and the combination equals 2b alone because word_recognition still runs one encode() step per agent. Combining is safe. THE BRANCH THAT WOULD NOT HAVE BEEN SAFE, recorded as a trap for any future serialization candidate: if the recognition trials are serialized into per-trial step() calls, the two become COMPLEMENTARY AND JOINTLY NECESSARY and serialization alone is insufficient -- the encode() turn's user message is word_list_text, the entire studied list formatted '{trial_index}: {word}', and it stays in conversation history for every subsequent trial turn -- so the studied list remains visible verbatim and the task stays leaky while appearing fixed. Either way A2's MEANING changes once the leak closes and the axis needs recalibration against a fresh baseline rather than a claimed delta.
interactions.2a_overflow: COMPLEMENTARY, plausibly necessary on nback. See P7. episodic_reset o 2a is the iteration-3 recommendation. On variable_mapping expect PARTLY REDUNDANT but super-additive in error count (displacement alone already tripled errors 12 -> 35), which is also where an rc_ratio near the human 1.386 first becomes arithmetically attainable, since the rc_ratio ceiling rises with error count.

offline_verification.verify_interface: PASS -- WorkingMemoryAgent rebound in 8 modules, MAX_KEYS in 10, encode/recall round trip returns expected shapes, capacity enforced at 4
offline_verification.stub_llm_leak_test: PASS -- all assertions. On the 5th letter turn of a 3-back block the context is exactly [system prompt] + [user: 'Your working memory currently contains:' + store + current letter] + the within-step tool loop. Max count of 'Next letter:' across all turns = 1; no earlier assistant reply present; the task instruction turn is absent (the system prompt carries the full rule via HUMAN_PROMPT_BY_N). On variable_mapping's question turn the store header appears exactly once, with no earlier statement block visible.
offline_verification.first_letter_turn: Inspected separately because it is the one turn at risk and the place P9 can fail. The store is still empty so the `if store` guard skips the state block: the agent sees exactly [system: prompt] + [user: 'Next letter: K'], with no state block and not even '(memory is empty)'. The guard is left as it is deliberately -- rendering an empty store would change encode()'s single step and destroy the byte-identical property in P10. Diagnostic pre-commitment: if P9 fails and the failure is localised to buffer-period turns, the reading is 'the agent lost track of sequence position', whose fix is pinning the instruction turn -- a DIFFERENT iteration-3 move from 'the reset broke the model'. model_parsed_buffer at n=1 is the live diagnostic for that (0.92 baseline, 1.00 displacement, 0.00 full_context), unlike n=3 where it is a fixed positional pattern and inert.
offline_verification.no_op_test: PASS -- encode()->recall() request streams byte-for-byte identical between baseline and episodic_reset
